newsitem.title: USA: Clinton-Jones case could be tried in a year -lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Clinton-Jones case could be tried in a year -lawyer.

text.p: One of the two lawyers representing Paula Jones in her sexual harassment lawsuit against U.S. President Bill Clinton predicted on Wednesday the case would go to trial in about a year.
Gilbert Davis, in an interview with NBC's "Today" show, also said Jones and her attorneys remained open to an out-of-court settlement under certain conditions.

"I think it will be about a year and the case will be tried," Davis said after the Supreme Court ruled unanimously on Tuesday that Jones's case against Clinton can proceed immediately rather than wait until he leaves office.

Davis said he, Jones and her other lawyer, Joseph Cammarata, remained open to a settlement but "the essential feature of any settlement would have to be a statement that would redeem her reputation, and that is non-negotiable.
"The particular language is something we could talk about but it would have to include that."
In a landmark ruling on Tuesday, all nine Supreme Court justices held for the first time that a lawsuit against a sitting president for conduct unrelated to official duties may proceed to trial.

The nation's highest court rejected Clinton's arguments that allowing the lawsuit to go forward while he remained in the White House would prove a significant distraction, hindering the performance of his presidential duties.

Jones accuses Clinton of making unwanted advances toward her in 1991 when he was governor of Arkansas and she was a state employee. Clinton denies the allegations. The Supreme Court made no ruling on the merits of her case, but said it should be allowed to proceed.

Jones contends that she took the legal action to clear her name after American Spectator published an article claiming that Arkansas state policemen set up sexual liaisons for Clinton. One of the women in the article was identified by the name "Paula." Jones alleged this tied her to the case.
